$comment: The starter catalogue (#190). One manifest read by the endpoint and by the tests, so a starter that ships uncovered is not possible. 'file' is the source in this repository; 'saveAs' is the name it takes in a project. Tiers are ordered; prompts within a tier are ordered. 'automation' (#212) is the wiring for a pipeline step: trigger, approval, output labels — the pipeline is catalogue content, never code. A tier that declares 'requires' (#229) is recognisable from a repository's own files, and installable only where a caller consents to it by name (#269). 'prerequisites' (#269) are the files a tier's prompts read but a fresh repository does not have: 'file' is the source here, 'path' is where it lands in the project, and the two are decoupled so a source name may differ from its target (one gitkeep source fills two directories). A prerequisite is written only where nothing exists at its path — an existing file always wins, which is what keeps a seeded document the project's own rather than a copy displacing one (ADR-0012, DEC-064 revising DEC-048).

tiers.title: The spec-first workflow
tiers.summary: The loop this product's own development runs on: an idea is interrogated to readiness, proposed as a spec, implemented against it, then closed out with a retro and one commit.
tiers.requires: OpenSpec, and the documents these prompts read — a definition of ready, a retro log, and the openspec/ directory layout. Consenting to this tier installs all of them alongside the prompts; anything you already have is left exactly as it is.

prompts.purpose: Interrogate a raw idea until it meets the definition of ready.
prompts.assumes: A definition-of-ready document, and product context to grill against.

prompts.purpose: Turn a ready issue into an OpenSpec proposal on a branch, as a draft pull request.
prompts.assumes: OpenSpec, and the spec-review gate as a lifecycle label.

prompts.purpose: Implement a validated proposal on its own branch and mark the pull request ready.
prompts.assumes: OpenSpec, a tasks.md convention, and a work-in-progress limit to check.

prompts.purpose: Close out an approved change: retro, archive, spec sync, then one squashed commit.
prompts.assumes: OpenSpec's specs and archive directories, and a retro log.

prompts.purpose: Record a finding that arrived after a change had already merged.
Report where every in-flight change actually is.
